name: Benguela Railway
subtitle: The Benguela Railway links the Atlantic port of Lobito with Luau on the Congo border, 1,344 km on the rebuilt line.

facts.label: Route and length
facts.value: Rebuilt line of 1,344 km between the port of Lobito and the DR Congo border

facts.label: Concession and opening
facts.value: Built under a 1902 concession agreement and opened in stages between 1908 and 1931; 1,067 mm gauge, 67 stations

facts.label: Civil war
facts.value: Operations disrupted from 1975; through traffic to DR Congo ceased in 1981

facts.label: State by 2001
facts.value: By the end of the concession in 2001 the line was wrecked; only the 34 km Benguela-Lobito section worked

facts.label: Rebuild
facts.value: China Railway Construction Corp rebuilt the line in stages; project completed August 2014

facts.label: Labour in rebuild
facts.value: Around 100,000 Angolans employed in reconstruction, 10,000 given specialist railway training

facts.label: Completion to Luau
facts.value: Completed to Luau in 1929, with a hiatus between 1913 and 1920

facts.label: Construction labour
facts.value: 7,000 men worked on the first decade, most of them from abroad, including Ghana and Liberia

facts.label: Extension to Katanga
facts.value: Described as 1,866 km long, connecting Lobito with Luau and then extending to the Katanga mining region in the Belgian Congo

facts.label: Destruction
facts.value: Civil war destroyed the line in 1983; Lobito-Luena link restored 2012

parts.text: The Benguela Railway links the Atlantic port of Lobito with Luau on the Congo border, 1,344 km on the rebuilt line. Construction began in 1903 and reached Luau in 1929. Civil war ended through traffic in 1981, and a Chinese-backed rebuild was completed in 2014.
